key_insight: Graphene on Ge(001)/Si(001) shows spatially varying electronic coupling and charge transfer that depends on the local nanofaceted interface, switching from n-type behavior in the pristine case to p-type under oxidation.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and controlling this interfacial doping landscape helps optimize graphene integration with silicon-compatible platforms and improve graphene transfer quality for device and protective-coating applications.
method: UPS and KPFM mapped work-function variations across the nanofaceted surface.
ARPES and DFT compared pristine versus oxidized interfaces to determine doping polarity.
STS data were classified with machine learning to separate local electronic regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent agreement between spectroscopy and DFT, plus ML-resolved STS regimes spanning nearly free-standing, strongly coupled, and nanoribbon-like regions.
watch_item: The oxidation state and local morphology strongly affect the observed doping, so interface preparation and environmental control are critical for reproducible device behavior.
paper_title: Electronic Coupling and Charge-Transfer Landscape of Graphene on Ge(001)/Si(001): Multiscale Analysis Assisted by Machine Learning
